entries.text: For every admitted package, two executions with the same public projection have equal normalized hostile-host observations outside the artifact-declared releases (status, plaintext return, encrypted-return ciphertext): exactly for the exact backends, and up to the Path ORAM storage relation on the proof-grade Path ORAM routes.

A production runtime accepts a call only under a current admitted-package identity, deployment policy hash match, return-channel session match, freshness evidence and the hash of the receipt it issued last, and answers with the next receipt of the deployment's chain; a replayed, reordered or skipped receipt does not follow.

entries.doc_anchor: Exact-UO is claimed for exact backends
entries.text: Exact-UO is claimed for the exact backends on the instrumented abstract/runtime model: UOCell, UOArray, and full-scan UOMap.

The bounded local-position-map Path ORAM route path_oram_local_posmap_v1 (capacity 128) executes; its Lean paper-main theorem holds over admitted configurations given bundle evidence, whose leaf obligation follows from the leaf model without seed enumeration, and the bundle is derived for a concrete single-access instance (SingleAccessMap.put) and, for the multi-access entrypoints, from one runtime run per side whose leaves are substituted for every other tape, with runtime runs on sampled tapes checked against the substitution.

The private-position-map Path ORAM route path_oram_private_posmap_v1 lifts the local route's capacity cap and keeps a map as an oblivious AVL tree of preallocated nodes in one Path ORAM tree, each node holding its children's leaves, so the position map recurses through the tree: a get makes h node accesses and a put 3h + 1, h the largest AVL height for the capacity, each reading and writing one path, and an operation reads and writes its header and stash pages once; a write also makes a get that finds whether its key is present, unless the program shows that the most recent access to the map is a get of the same key, whose presence it reuses; its Lean paper-main theorem holds over admitted configurations whose maps use either scheme, given the same bundle evidence, with the stash bounded by the Path ORAM bound plus the 3h + 1 nodes an operation returns to it (stashOverflowBounded), and the bundle is derived for ERC20Lite.transferFrom with balances on the private scheme from one runtime run per side whose leaves are substituted for every other tape, with runtime runs on sampled tapes checked against the substitution.

On both Path ORAM routes, the paper-main theorems' public outcome, boundary schedule, final public-state record and release premises are discharged for entrypoints whose kernel program is admitted, from the same kernel models as on the exact route, given a denotation of the admitted configurations as admitted kernel runs that keeps the public projection; the modeled boundary schedule leaves and re-enters the enclave around each of the call's ORAM accesses, whose number the program and its maps' schemes fix. The runtime's outcomes, boundary schedules and final records are checked against the models on every Path ORAM experiment run, not proved to follow them.

The private scheme's AVL map algorithm, modeled over inductive trees with the runtime's walk, successor delete, rotation rule and node-access counts, implements a finite map: with the walk bounded by the capacity's largest AVL height, a get returns the key's value and a put writes, updates or deletes it, keeps the tree sorted, balanced and within the capacity, and overflows exactly when it would insert into a full map; the runtime's tree_get and tree_put are replayed against the model, not proved to follow it.

Which lookups of a Path ORAM map in a call reuse the fact an earlier lookup of the same key found, a value or on the private scheme a presence, is a function of the program: over a straight-line body's events every run makes the plan's lookups and reuses the plan's facts, whatever the values of its variables and of what it binds, and every lookup that reuses a fact has, in every run, the key the fact was found under. That the compiler, uo-check, the Lean translation checker and the runtime follow the plan is checked by the translation checker, the runtime's tests and the tamper suite, not proved of the Rust code.

That a runtime run of a call on another tape is the representative run with that tape's leaves substituted, which the tape-family theorems take from one runtime run, is tested and not proved of the Rust runtime: on maps of both Path ORAM schemes at three capacities each, calls of seven kinds (a read that hits, one that misses, an insert, an overwrite, a delete, a delete of an absent key and a write that aborts), each after a setup with deletes and aborts, run on 16 other deployment seeds each, and the Lean checker finds every one of the 1,344 runs equal to the substituted run.

The backend planner's model of the bytes of sealed records a call moves is tested, not proved: maps of three key and value widths on the full scan and both Path ORAM schemes, at seven capacities and up to three occupancy levels, move in every read of a stored or an absent key, overwrite and insert exactly the bytes the model gives their backend; every backend that can hold a map is measured and every other is rejected with its predicted diagnostic; at six shares of reads the planner chooses the backend whose measured calls moved the fewest bytes, with every competitor present; and a map compiled with backend auto, with or without an enclave memory budget, is on the backend its plan chose and moves the bytes of its model, while a budget no backend fits does not compile. The planner minimizes modeled bytes, not time; its enclave memory is modeled, not measured; and its model call reads or writes a map once.

The artifact-level admitted-package hash is a canonical SHA-256 binding over source-language tag, semantics-profile tag, source bytes, sidecar metadata, compilation mode, compiler version, toolchain digest, and package schema tag.

Every artifact declares the executable-semantics profile tag uo-evm-modular256-v1, bound into the admitted-package hash, pinning the executable divergences from Solidity 0.8; the proof-grade checker rejects an unknown or divergent profile.

The source-backed runtime implementation boundaries are source-frozen/static-drift evidence, not a full semantics-of-Rust refinement; proof-critical obligations may not rest solely on a source regression.

Every sealed record the runtime opens or seals crosses to a storage adapter, which logs the read with the record it keeps and the write with the class it computes from its own records. On every benchmark and sealed backend the adapter's writes are the trace's writes of sealed objects, each an Update, and its reads are the trace's reads, one for one: a Path ORAM map's counter and metadata pages once, where the call loads the map, and the buckets of each access. A runtime restarted from the adapter's files answers as before and repeats no nonce, and the restart takes the files only at the attested commit generation or one past it, which every commit, a committed abort's too, advances. A store in files fails closed: after an append to its journal fails, it refuses every operation until its files are opened again, a call whose commit failed returns an error whose outcome is unknown and no receipt, and the files hold every call that returned and the failed one whole or not at all, which a restart resolves; every failure a file store can be made to meet is run on ERC20Lite's sealed backends and, in the production build, through the production runtime. Empirically tested over the benchmarks; the places where a record crosses are source-frozen.
uo-solc admits the uo-solidity-like-dsl-v1 subset and rejects every unsupported feature with a diagnostic that names it; admission is empirically exercised, not a semantic proof.

Executable insecure raw baselines (insecure-eval-raw) run confidential work on raw backends to measure overhead and leakage; they are evaluation-only and never admitted by the proof-grade or deployment paths.

entries.text: bucketEncryptionINDCPA: hides Path ORAM bucket/path ciphertext contents; named in Lean and not formalized (a Prop field that no proof uses and the checkers fill with True), grounded in the runtime ChaCha20Poly1305 sealed-record boundary.
metadataEncryptionINDCPA: hides encrypted position-map metadata pages; named in Lean and not formalized, paired with the same sealed-record crypto route.
stashOverflowBounded: bounds Path ORAM stash failure for deployed parameters; named in Lean and not formalized, paired with the JACM stash theorem at Z = 5 and pinned parameters.

Runtime key derivation: each object's storage key, initial placement and Path ORAM leaf coins derive from a 256-bit master secret from the OS by HKDF-SHA256, one label per use, and the ChaCha20 generator; trusted and not modeled in Lean, with the derivation's call sites pinned by the runtime boundary validation.

Return-channel AEAD: a value returned under encrypted_to_client is hidden from the host by ChaCha20Poly1305 under the session key, with associated data that bind the package, the entrypoint, the public arguments and the session, and a nonce hashed from the runtime's freshness counters; the theorems erase the ciphertext and the tag as a declared release, so the assumption is trusted and not named in Lean, and the session key comes from an attested key exchange the repository does not implement.

Production receipt MAC: a receipt's tag is HMAC-SHA256 under a key that HKDF-SHA256 derives from the session key and id; that a receipt and a tag an adversary of the session outputs, whose tag verifies, have the hash of a receipt the runtime issued (UnforgeableAgainst), and that the adversary outputs no receipt but an issued one with the SHA-256 hash of an issued receipt (HashBindsIssued), are the hypotheses of deployment_receipt_tag_verifies_issued, trusted and not proved; both hold in a model in which the runtime did not issue a receipt the adversary outputs (deployment_receipt_tag_assumptions_not_vacuous); and the session key comes from an attested key exchange the repository does not implement.

TEE deployment assumptions: enclave memory confidentiality/integrity, attestation authenticity, rollback resistance (a monotonic counter that follows the store's commit generation, advanced before a call's result is released), freshness, crash recovery, patch-level trust, and platform sealing; explicit Lean bundle SgxDeploymentAssumptions.
Parser/preprocessing equivalence: connects raw Solidity-like source text to the post-resolution AST consumed by Lean; still a trusted front-end surface.
Real Keccak equivalence: connects runtime tiny_keccak Keccak::v256() to the Lean mock-hash abstraction; not yet proved, Lean preservation uses the shared abstraction.

entries.doc_anchor: the detection, at a restart, of a store that was rolled back together
entries.text: Not claimed: the detection, at a restart, of a store that was rolled back together with the attested generation, of two stores that one generation names (a commit whose result was not released, set aside by a restart from the files before it, or two instances restarted from the same files), or of a store that holds an older record of a location. A restart compares the store's commit generation with the attested one; that the platform's counter follows the generation and is not rolled back is the rollback resistance of the TEE deployment assumptions.
Not claimed: downstream machine-code equivalence below the checked runtime boundary. Would require additional models and proofs.
Not claimed: a complete semantics-of-Rust refinement for every residual implementation detail.
